# Design: drug (D1-3) vs vehicle (V1-3), 3 independent cultures per arm, no batch info.
# Scale: TPM (normalized, no raw counts) -> log2(TPM+1), limma (lm + eBayes, trend=TRUE).
#   No DESeq2/edgeR/voom (need counts). TPM is not corrected for composition bias (no TMM).
# Data-reading choices: keep genes with TPM>=1 in >=3 samples (filter independent of arm labels' contrast
#   direction but reads expression); BH correction across tested genes, threshold 0.05.
suppressMessages(library(limma))
dir.create("output", showWarnings=FALSE)
x <- read.delim("/analysis-001/data/inputs/f-expr/expression_tpm.tsv", check.names=FALSE)
meta <- read.csv("/analysis-001/data/inputs/f-meta/samples.csv")
cat("dims", dim(x), "NA cells:", sum(is.na(x[,meta$sample])), "dup ids:", sum(duplicated(x$gene_id)), "\n")
m <- as.matrix(x[, meta$sample]); rownames(m) <- x$gene_id
stopifnot(all(colnames(m) == meta$sample))
m[!is.na(m) & m < 0] <- NA
keep <- rowSums(m >= 1, na.rm=TRUE) >= 3 & rowSums(!is.na(m)) >= 4
cat("genes kept", sum(keep), "of", nrow(m), "\n")
l <- log2(m[keep, ] + 1)
arm <- factor(meta$arm, levels=c("vehicle","drug"))
design <- model.matrix(~ arm)
fit <- eBayes(lmFit(l, design), trend=TRUE, robust=TRUE)   # lmFit handles NA per gene
tt <- topTable(fit, coef="armdrug", number=Inf, sort.by="P", confint=TRUE)
tt$gene_id <- rownames(tt)
tt$symbol <- x$symbol[match(tt$gene_id, x$gene_id)]
res <- data.frame(gene_id=tt$gene_id, symbol=tt$symbol,
  mean_tpm_drug=rowMeans(m[tt$gene_id, meta$arm=="drug"], na.rm=TRUE),
  mean_tpm_vehicle=rowMeans(m[tt$gene_id, meta$arm=="vehicle"], na.rm=TRUE),
  log2_fold_change=tt$logFC, ci_lower=tt$CI.L, ci_upper=tt$CI.R,
  mean_log2_tpm=tt$AveExpr, t_statistic=tt$t, pvalue=tt$P.Value, adjusted_pvalue=tt$adj.P.Val)
write.csv(res, "output/de_drug_vs_vehicle.csv", row.names=FALSE)
cat("padj<0.05:", sum(res$adjusted_pvalue < 0.05), " & |log2FC|>1:", sum(res$adjusted_pvalue<0.05 & abs(res$log2_fold_change)>1),
    " up:", sum(res$adjusted_pvalue<0.05 & res$log2_fold_change>0), "\n")
print(summary(res$log2_fold_change)); print(head(res, 8))

results.text:
Of the 300 genes, 25 are higher in the drug arm than in the vehicle arm (adjusted p < 0.05), and none are lower. Treat this as provisional, because the data look unusual (see the flags below).

**What I ran:** the input was TPM only, with no raw counts, so DESeq2 and edgeR were not valid. I used limma on log2(TPM+1) with the trend and robust options, comparing drug (D1–D3) with vehicle (V1–V3). I used Benjamini-Hochberg correction across all 300 genes. All 300 passed my expression filter (TPM ≥ 1 in at least 3 samples), so nothing was removed. The script is `scripts/de.R` and the log is `logs/de.log`.

**Results** (`output/de_drug_vs_vehicle.csv`, with log2 fold change, 95% CI, p-value and adjusted p-value for every gene):
- 25 genes have adjusted p < 0.05. All 25 are up in the drug arm, and 24 of them also have |log2 fold change| > 1.
- Those up-regulated genes all sit at a log2 fold change of about 1.625, roughly 3.1-fold. The top one is GENE21, at 1.625 (95% CI 1.48–1.77, adjusted p = 4.8e-91).
- The other 275 genes show log2 fold changes of about ±0.048 and none are significant.

**Flags:**
- **Unusually uniform effects.** Every up-regulated gene has the same fold change, and the remaining genes are flat. That pattern looks like a gene-set-wide scaling or synthetic data, not typical gene-by-gene biology. I would check how the data were generated or processed before interpreting individual genes.
- **Extreme p-values.** Values around 1e-90 with only 3 replicates per arm come from near-zero variance between replicates, so rank genes by fold change and its confidence interval rather than by p-value. Replicates within an arm are also almost identical, for example D1 and D3, and V1 and V3.
- **TPM instead of counts.** The statistics are approximate. TPM is not corrected for composition bias, and a few strongly up genes can shift the apparent level of all the others.
- **Sample sheet.** It has no batch or culture-pairing information, so I could not model either.

I made no figures because the task asked only for the per-gene table.

"""ORA of GO:BP (MSigDB C5 GO BP 2024.1) on genes carrying DMPs (FDR<0.05, DSS, from T1S1).
Design: unit = gene; hits = genes with >=1 significant DMP; background = the 220 genes
with tested CpGs (T1S1). Gene sets restricted to background; size filter 15-500 applied
to the set after intersecting with background. Hypergeometric test, BH over tested sets.
Caveat: genes with more CpGs tested have more chance of a DMP (not corrected here).
"""
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from scipy.stats import hypergeom
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests

D = "/analysis-001/runs/run-001/T1S1/output/"
GMT = "/mnt/refs/go/c5.go.bp.v2024.1.Hs.symbols.gmt"
MIN, MAX = 15, 500

dmp = pd.read_csv(D + "dmp_results.csv")
bg = set(pd.read_csv(D + "tested_cpgs_per_gene.csv").gene)
hits = set(dmp.gene) & bg
print("DMP sites", len(dmp), "hit genes", len(hits), "background", len(bg))

rows = []
for line in open(GMT):
    p = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
    gs = set(p[2:]) & bg
    n_full = len(p) - 2
    rows.append((p[0], n_full, gs))
tested = [(t, nf, gs) for t, nf, gs in rows if MIN <= len(gs) <= MAX]
print("gene sets total", len(rows), "tested after size filter", len(tested))

N, K = len(bg), len(hits)
out = []
for t, nf, gs in tested:
    ov = gs & hits
    k, m = len(ov), len(gs)
    pv = hypergeom.sf(k - 1, N, m, K) if k > 0 else 1.0
    out.append(dict(term=t, source="MSigDB C5 GO:BP 2024.1", set_size_in_background=m,
                    overlap=k, fold_enrichment=(k / K) / (m / N) if k else 0,
                    pvalue=pv, genes=";".join(sorted(ov))))
res = pd.DataFrame(out)
if len(res):
    res["adjusted_pvalue"] = multipletests(res.pvalue, method="fdr_bh")[1]
    res = res.sort_values("pvalue")
res.to_csv("output/go_bp_ora_results.csv", index=False)
print(res.head(15).to_string() if len(res) else "no testable sets")
print("FDR<0.05:", int((res.adjusted_pvalue < 0.05).sum()) if len(res) else 0)

results.text:
Two GO biological process terms are enriched among the genes with differentially methylated sites. This is weak evidence, because the staged GO file holds only 12 terms, not the full ontology (details below).

**Method.** I ran over-representation analysis on the hit genes against the staged MSigDB C5 GO:BP 2024.1 file. The hits are the 53 genes with at least one site at FDR < 0.05, covering 108 sites. The background is the 220 genes with tested CpGs, not the whole genome. I used a hypergeometric test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction across the 12 terms.

| GO term | Genes in background | Hit genes in term | Fold enrichment | p-value | Adjusted p-value |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| GOBP_RESPONSE_TO_HYPOXIA | 30 | 18 | 2.49 | 6e-6 | 6.6e-5 |
| GOBP_SYNAPTIC_SIGNALING | 36 | 19 | 2.19 | 3.9e-5 | 2.4e-4 |

The other 10 terms are not enriched (adjusted p ≥ 0.83). They include cell cycle process, apoptosis regulation, inflammatory response and angiogenesis. The full table with overlap genes is in `output/go_bp_ora_results.csv`. The script is `scripts/go_ora.py`.

**Caveats**
- **Only 12 GO terms were tested.** The staged file is `/mnt/refs/go/c5.go.bp.v2024.1.Hs.symbols.gmt`, and it holds only 12 gene sets, each with 20 to 36 genes in the background. The multiple-testing burden is therefore tiny, and "enriched" only means enriched relative to these 12 terms. I could not check this against a full GO annotation. Some memberships also look unusual: the hypoxia set includes INS, GH1 and CD8A. Please verify the reference file before relying on the biology.
- **Gene-level bias was not corrected.** Genes with more CpGs tested, such as ACTB with 112, are more likely to carry a significant site. This can inflate enrichment for terms that contain such genes. ACTB is a hit in the synaptic signaling term. I did not weight the test by CpG count or split hypo- and hypermethylated sites.
- **The 220-gene panel looks pre-selected.** Because it is not genome-wide, the enrichment is relative to that panel only.
- The result is an association. It does not show that methylation changes drive these processes.

"""GO BP over-representation of genes carrying DMPs (DSS, FDR<0.05; T1S1).
Design: unranked gene list (genes with >=1 significant CpG), 2-sided direction pooled.
Background: the 220 genes with covered CpGs (tested_cpgs_per_gene.csv), not the genome.
Gene sets: MSigDB C5 GO:BP 2024.1 (human symbols). Size filter 15-500 on the full set (before
background intersection); additionally >=3 set genes in background and overlap>=2 to be testable.
Test: one-sided hypergeometric, BH FDR over all tested sets. Threshold FDR<0.05.
Caveat: gene-level ORA ignores the number of CpGs per gene (genes with many CpGs are more
likely hits); this is not corrected here.
"""
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from scipy.stats import hypergeom
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

T1 = "/analysis-001/runs/run-001/T1S1/output/"
GMT = "/mnt/refs/go/c5.go.bp.v2024.1.Hs.symbols.gmt"
dmp = pd.read_csv(T1 + "dmp_results.csv")
bg = set(pd.read_csv(T1 + "tested_cpgs_per_gene.csv").gene)
hits = set(dmp.gene) & bg
assert set(dmp.gene) <= bg, "hit genes outside background"
N, n = len(bg), len(hits)
rows = []
for line in open(GMT):
    p = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
    name, genes = p[0], set(p[2:])
    if not 15 <= len(genes) <= 500: continue
    gb = genes & bg
    ov = gb & hits
    if len(gb) < 3 or len(ov) < 2: continue
    pv = hypergeom.sf(len(ov) - 1, N, len(gb), n)
    rows.append(dict(term=name, source="MSigDB C5 GO:BP 2024.1", set_size=len(genes),
                     set_size_in_background=len(gb), overlap=len(ov),
                     fold_enrichment=(len(ov) / n) / (len(gb) / N), pvalue=pv,
                     genes=";".join(sorted(ov))))
res = pd.DataFrame(rows)
res["adjusted_pvalue"] = multipletests(res.pvalue, method="fdr_bh")[1]
res = res.sort_values("pvalue")
res.to_csv("output/go_bp_enrichment.csv", index=False)
print(f"hits={n} background={N} tested_sets={len(res)} sig={int((res.adjusted_pvalue<0.05).sum())}")
print(res.head(15)[["term", "overlap", "set_size_in_background", "pvalue", "adjusted_pvalue"]].to_string())

top = res.head(15).iloc[::-1]
plt.style.use("seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 6))
sc = ax.scatter(top.fold_enrichment, range(len(top)), s=top.overlap * 25,
                c=-np.log10(top.adjusted_pvalue), cmap="viridis")
ax.set_yticks(range(len(top))); ax.set_yticklabels([t[:55] for t in top.term], fontsize=7)
ax.set_xlabel("Fold enrichment"); ax.set_title("GO BP ORA of DMP genes (top 15 by p-value)")
plt.colorbar(sc, label="-log10 adjusted p-value")
plt.tight_layout()
for e in ("png", "pdf"): plt.savefig(f"figures/go_bp_dotplot.{e}", dpi=300)

results.text:
Two GO biological processes are enriched among the 53 genes with differentially methylated sites: response to hypoxia and synaptic signaling. Both pass FDR < 0.05, and the other 10 terms tested do not.

I ran an over-representation test on the 53 genes with at least one site at FDR < 0.05. The background was the 220 genes with CpG coverage, not the whole genome. The gene sets were MSigDB GO:BP 2024.1 with the usual 15–500 size filter. I used a one-sided hypergeometric test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction across all 12 sets tested.

| GO term | Overlap (hit genes / background genes in the set) | p-value | Adjusted p-value |
|-|-|-|-|
| Response to hypoxia | 18 / 30 | 6e-6 | 6.6e-5 |
| Synaptic signaling | 19 / 36 | 3.9e-5 | 2.4e-4 |

The other 10 terms have adjusted p-values of 0.83–0.90. They include cell cycle, apoptosis regulation, inflammatory response, angiogenesis, Wnt signaling and chromatin organization.

Caveats:
- **Few terms were testable.** The GO file yielded only 12 sets that met the size and overlap rules against this 220-gene background. The two hits are therefore a narrow result, not a genome-wide GO survey.
- **The background is a targeted gene panel.** Of its 220 genes, 24% (53) are hits.
- **The test is gene-level.** It ignores how many CpGs were tested per gene, and genes with many CpGs are more likely to be hits. I did not correct for this, so the enrichment could partly reflect that bias.
- **Direction is pooled.** Hyper- and hypomethylated sites are combined, so the result doesn't say whether hypoxia genes gain or lose methylation.
- **This is an association, not a mechanism.** I did not collapse redundant GO terms because only two passed.

- output/go_bp_enrichment.csv
- figures/go_bp_dotplot.png
- figures/go_bp_dotplot.pdf

# Design: ORA of genes carrying FDR<0.05 DMPs (T1S1) vs. background = all 220 genes with tested CpGs.
# Gene sets: MSigDB C5 GO:BP 2024.1 (human symbols). Size filter 15-500 on full set; sets must have >=3 genes in
# background. Fisher exact (one-sided), BH over all tested sets. Gene-level test: genes with more CpGs are more likely hits (not corrected).
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from scipy.stats import fisher_exact
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests
d=pd.read_csv('/analysis-001/runs/run-001/T1S1/output/dmp_results.csv')
bg=set(pd.read_csv('/analysis-001/runs/run-001/T1S1/output/tested_cpgs_per_gene.csv').gene)

for l in open('/mnt/refs/go/c5.go.bp.v2024.1.Hs.symbols.gmt'):

    if not 15<=len(g)<=500: continue
    gb=g&bg; k=len(gb&hits)
    if len(gb)<3 or k<2: continue
    a=k;b=len(hits)-k;c=len(gb)-k;e=len(bg)-len(hits)-c
    _,pv=fisher_exact([[a,b],[c,e]],alternative='greater')
    rows.append(dict(term=p[0],source='GO:BP MSigDB 2024.1',set_size=len(g),size_in_background=len(gb),overlap=k,
      fold_enrichment=(k/len(hits))/(len(gb)/len(bg)),pvalue=pv,genes=';'.join(sorted(gb&hits))))
r=pd.DataFrame(rows)
r['adjusted_pvalue']=multipletests(r.pvalue,method='fdr_bh')[1]
r=r.sort_values('pvalue'); r.to_csv('output/go_bp_enrichment_all.csv',index=False)
r[r.adjusted_pvalue<0.05].to_csv('output/go_bp_enrichment_significant.csv',index=False)
print(len(hits),len(bg),len(r),(r.adjusted_pvalue<0.05).sum())
print(r.head(15)[['term','overlap','size_in_background','pvalue','adjusted_pvalue']].to_string())
EOF

results.text:
Yes, the genes at the smoking-associated sites share two biological processes. Both pass FDR < 0.05, but the evidence is thin.

| GO:BP term | Hit genes in term | Background genes in term | p-value | Adjusted p-value (BH) |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| Response to hypoxia | 18 | 30 | 6×10⁻⁶ | 6.6×10⁻⁵ |
| Synaptic signaling | 19 | 36 | 3.9×10⁻⁵ | 2.4×10⁻⁴ |

The other 10 terms tested are not significant (adjusted p ≥ 0.83). They include cell cycle, apoptosis regulation, inflammatory response and angiogenesis.

**Method**
- **Test:** over-representation analysis (one-sided Fisher exact test) on the 53 genes that carry at least one site at FDR < 0.05 in T1S1.
- **Background:** the 220 genes with CpGs tested in T1S1, not the whole genome.
- **Gene sets:** MSigDB C5 GO Biological Process 2024.1. I kept sets of 15–500 genes, with at least 3 genes in the background and at least 2 hits.
- **Correction:** BH over the 12 sets that qualified.

**Caveats**
- **Few terms tested:** only 12 sets passed the filters. The gene list is a curated panel of 220 genes, not a genome-wide set, so the background is already enriched for particular biology.
- **Gene-level test:** a gene with many tested CpGs is more likely to have a significant site. For example, ACTB has 112 tested CpGs. I did not correct for this, so large genes can inflate enrichment.
- **Hypoxia and synaptic terms:** both are large relative to the 53 hits, so some of this signal may come from a few well-covered genes. I did not check this.
- **Not mechanistic:** this is a statistical association between hit genes and GO terms. It is not evidence that smoking acts through these processes. Direction of methylation change is not separated here.

Files are in `/analysis-001/runs/run-001/T1S2`:
- `output/go_bp_enrichment_significant.csv`
- `output/go_bp_enrichment_all.csv`
- `scripts/ora_go.py`

# Design: gene-level ORA of genes carrying significant DMPs (DSS, FDR<0.05, from T1S1).
# Background = the 220 genes with tested CpGs (T1S1 tested_cpgs_per_gene.csv).
# Gene sets: MSigDB C5 GO:BP 2024.1 (human symbols), restricted to background genes, size 15-500 (after restriction to background
# is too strict for a 220-gene universe, so size is applied on the full set (15-500) and overlap with background must be >=2).
# Test: one-sided hypergeometric, BH over all tested terms. Direction not split (too few genes).
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from scipy.stats import hypergeom
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests
D = "/analysis-001/runs/run-001/T1S1/output/"
dmp = pd.read_csv(D + "dmp_results.csv")
tested = pd.read_csv(D + "tested_cpgs_per_gene.csv")
bg = set(tested.gene)
hits = set(dmp.gene) & bg
N, n = len(bg), len(hits)
rows = []
for line in open("/mnt/refs/go/c5.go.bp.v2024.1.Hs.symbols.gmt"):
    f = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
    genes = set(f[2:])
    if not 15 <= len(genes) <= 500: continue
    gb = genes & bg
    ov = gb & hits
    if len(gb) < 2 or len(ov) < 2: continue
    p = hypergeom.sf(len(ov) - 1, N, len(gb), n)
    rows.append(dict(term=f[0], source="GO:BP MSigDB 2024.1", set_size=len(genes), size_in_background=len(gb),
                     overlap=len(ov), fold_enrichment=(len(ov)/n)/(len(gb)/N), pvalue=p, genes=";".join(sorted(ov))))
# FDR family = all terms with >=2 background genes (including those with <2 hits)
allp = []
for line in open("/mnt/refs/go/c5.go.bp.v2024.1.Hs.symbols.gmt"):
    f = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t"); g = set(f[2:])
    if 15 <= len(g) <= 500 and len(g & bg) >= 2:
        allp.append(hypergeom.sf(len(g & hits) - 1, N, len(g & bg), n) if len(g & hits) >= 1 else 1.0)
m = len(allp)
res = pd.DataFrame(rows)
adj = multipletests(allp, method="fdr_bh")[1]
order = np.argsort(allp)
# map BH adjustment: recompute for result rows from the full family
allp_arr = np.array(allp); 
res["adjusted_pvalue"] = [min(1, p * m / (1 + (allp_arr < p).sum())) for p in res.pvalue]
res = res.sort_values("pvalue")
# monotone BH
res["adjusted_pvalue"] = np.minimum.accumulate(res["adjusted_pvalue"][::-1])[::-1].clip(upper=1)
res.to_csv("output/go_bp_enrichment_all.csv", index=False)
sig = res[res.adjusted_pvalue < 0.05]
sig.to_csv("output/go_bp_enrichment_significant.csv", index=False)
print(f"hit genes {n}, background {N}, terms tested {m}, significant {len(sig)}")
print(res.head(15)[["term","overlap","size_in_background","pvalue","adjusted_pvalue"]].to_string())

results.text:
Yes, partly. Two of the 12 GO biological process terms I could test are enriched at FDR < 0.05: response to hypoxia and synaptic signaling.

| GO:BP term | Hit genes / tested genes in term | p-value | Adjusted p-value (BH) |
|-|-|-|-|
| Response to hypoxia | 18 / 30 | 6e-6 | 6.6e-5 |
| Synaptic signaling | 19 / 36 | 3.9e-5 | 2.4e-4 |

The other 10 terms are not significant (adjusted p = 0.90). They include cell cycle, apoptosis regulation, inflammatory response, angiogenesis, Wnt signaling and chromatin organization.

**Method:** I ran an over-representation test (one-sided hypergeometric). The 53 genes carrying a significant smoking-associated CpG (FDR < 0.05, from T1S1) were tested against the 220 genes with tested CpGs as the background. Gene sets came from MSigDB GO:BP 2024.1 (size 15–500). Multiple-testing correction covered all 12 terms. I did not split hypermethylated and hypomethylated sites, because there are too few genes.

**Caveats:**
- **CpG count per gene:** Genes with many tested CpGs are more likely to contain a significant site. For example, ACTB has 112 tested CpGs. This bias is not corrected, so the enrichment could partly reflect gene length and CpG density.
- **Small set of terms:** The GO file yielded only 12 terms with enough genes in this 220-gene background. The 220 genes look pre-selected, which would make the background narrow and the correction light. The result also says nothing about processes outside those 12 terms.
- **Overlap between terms:** The two significant terms may share genes, and I did not check this.
- **Interpretation:** Enrichment is an association. It does not show that these processes mediate the effects of smoking.

Files are in `/analysis-001/runs/run-001/T1S2`:
- `output/go_bp_enrichment_significant.csv`
- `output/go_bp_enrichment_all.csv`
- `scripts/go_ora.py`

Four approved drugs came back from ChEMBL: ruxolitinib, tofacitinib and baricitinib (JAK1 and JAK2), and deucravacitinib (TYK2). The list is probably incomplete. I wrote the table to `output/approved_jak_tyk2_drugs.csv` with `scripts/write_table.py`.

| Deucravacitinib | TYK2 | TYK2 inhibitor | CHEMBL4435170 against CHEMBL3553 (TYK2) |

All four are marked max phase 4 in ChEMBL. The first approvals ChEMBL lists are ruxolitinib 2011 (myelofibrosis), tofacitinib 2012 (rheumatoid arthritis), baricitinib 2018 (rheumatoid arthritis) and deucravacitinib 2022 (plaque psoriasis). In the CSV, each drug has one row per target.

**Gaps and limits:**
- **Missing drugs:** ChEMBL returned no record for upadacitinib, abrocitinib, fedratinib, pacritinib, momelotinib, ritlecitinib, filgotinib, delgocitinib or peficitinib, by drug name or compound search. I did not search ChEMBL for oclacitinib or ropeginterferon beyond the first name lookup, which also found nothing. Several of these are approved JAK inhibitors, so their absence reflects this ChEMBL lookup, not their regulatory status.
- **DGIdb:** It returned no records for JAK1, JAK2 or TYK2, so it gives no second source. Each row rests on one ChEMBL mechanism record.
- **Target-side query:** The ChEMBL mechanism query by target also came back empty. I used mechanism lookups by drug ID instead.
- **Scope of the CSV:** I fetched mechanism records only for the four drugs listed. It records the drug-to-target link, not any effect in this study's data.
- **Approval status:** The table infers approval from ChEMBL max phase 4 and the first-approval year. I did not check FDA or EMA records.
- **Release and transcription:** I did not capture the ChEMBL release version. The CSV values were typed into the script from lookups made during this step.
